name: Dependent Prepositions
summary: Fixed verb, noun and adjective + preposition combinations.

paragraphs: Some words always travel with a particular preposition. We say interested in, not interested on; depend on, not depend of; responsible for, not responsible of. These fixed partners are called dependent prepositions, because the preposition depends on the word before it.

There is usually no logical reason why a word takes one preposition and not another, which is why even advanced learners make mistakes. The good news is that a fairly small group of combinations appears again and again in IELTS writing. Learn these as chunks, and you will avoid most errors.

blocks.title: The rule in one line
blocks.text: Learn the word and its preposition together, as one chunk: depend on, responsible for, an increase in.

paragraphs: Preposition errors rarely stop the examiner from understanding you, but they appear often and make writing look less natural. Many high-frequency IELTS phrases, such as have an impact on, lead to and contribute to, depend on getting the preposition right.
Task 1 has its own important set: an increase in, a rise of 10%, rose to 50% and rose by 10%. Choosing the wrong one can even change the meaning of the data you are reporting.

Many verbs need a fixed preposition before their object. You cannot choose the preposition by meaning; you simply have to know it. The table below shows the combinations that appear most often in Task 2 essays.
A good habit is to learn new verbs in short phrases, such as rely on public transport, rather than as single words.

rows: Many families rely on one income.
Schools should focus on practical skills.
Poor diet can result in obesity.
Governments should invest in public transport.
Teachers must deal with large classes.
Students should take part in sports.
Coal accounts for half of all electricity.

paragraphs: Adjectives also have fixed partners. These are very common in Task 2, where you describe people's attitudes, abilities and responsibilities.
Notice the pair different from and similar to. They are opposites in meaning, and they take different prepositions.

rows: Parents are responsible for their children.
Many students are interested in science.
People are more aware of health risks.
Many people are worried about pollution.
Some children are good at sports.
The figures were similar to those in 2010.
City life is very different from village life.
People are proud of their culture.

items.text: She is responsible of the project.
She is responsible for the project.

paragraphs: Nouns follow the same pattern. Some of the most useful nouns in academic writing, such as impact, effect, solution and access, are often paired with the wrong preposition.
Notice that the verb affect has no preposition (Smoking affects health), while the noun effect takes on (Smoking has an effect on health).

rows: Social media has an impact on teenagers.
There is a growing demand for housing.
Many villages lack access to clean water.
There was an increase in sales.
Stress is a major cause of illness.

items.text: the effect of smoking to health
the effect of smoking on health

sections.title: Rule 4: Verbs that take no preposition
sections.label: Rule 4: Verbs that take no preposition

paragraphs: Knowing when not to use a preposition is just as important. Several common verbs take a direct object, but learners often add a preposition because the verb feels similar to another one.
For example, discuss feels like talk about, so learners write discuss about. But discuss already includes the meaning of about.

sections.title: Rule 5: Task 1 prepositions: in, of, to, by
sections.label: Rule 5: Task 1 prepositions: in, of, to, by

paragraphs: Task 1 uses a small set of prepositions to describe changes, and each one has a precise job. In shows what changed, of gives the size of the change after a noun, by gives the size of the change after a verb, and to gives the final figure.
Mixing these up can change the meaning: rose to 20% and rose by 20% are not the same thing.

rows: size of the change (after a noun)
size of the change (after a verb)

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Prices rose by 20% means they went up by that amount. Prices rose to 20% means 20% was the new figure.

paragraphs: Dates and time periods also need the right preposition. Years, months and decades take in, specific days take on, and periods with two end points take between… and or from… to.
The mixed form between 2000 to 2010 is one of the most common Task 1 errors. Between always pairs with and; from always pairs with to.

rows: over the period, during the decade

paragraphs: When a verb comes directly after a preposition, it must be in the -ing form. This includes many dependent prepositions: interested in learning, responsible for keeping, instead of driving.
The tricky one is to. In phrases such as look forward to, be used to and contribute to, to is a preposition, so it is followed by a noun or an -ing form, not the base verb.

items.text: She is interested in study abroad.
She is interested in studying abroad.
This will contribute to reduce pollution.
This will contribute to reducing pollution.
Instead of driving, more people should cycle.

paragraphs: Many linking phrases used in essays contain fixed prepositions. Because they appear so often, mistakes in them are very noticeable to an examiner.
Learn them exactly as they are written, as complete chunks.
Here is how dependent prepositions appear in real IELTS writing.

rows: There was a sharp increase in house prices.
The figures were similar to those in 2010.
Social media has a strong influence on young people.
Governments should invest in renewable energy.
This essay will discuss both views.

paragraphs: These five errors are among the most common preposition mistakes in IELTS essays.
Use this routine on every preposition in your final check.

steps: Find each preposition and the word just before it.
Ask: is this a fixed pair I know? If not, check it against the tables.
Look for extra prepositions after discuss, emphasize, affect, reach and lack.

furtherStudy.title: Purdue OWL: Prepositions for Time, Place and Introducing Objects
furtherStudy.description: A clear guide to common preposition patterns.

cards.front: Many families depend ____ farming for their income.
cards.why: Depend always takes on: depend on something.

cards.front: Parents are responsible ____ their children's safety.
Social media has a strong impact ____ teenagers.
cards.why: The nouns impact, effect and influence take on.

cards.front: We discussed ____ the new timetable in class.
cards.why: Discuss takes a direct object. The meaning of about is already inside discuss.

cards.front: There was a sharp increase ____ house prices.
cards.why: After increase, use in for what changed. Of is used for the size: an increase of 10%.
The change was 20%, so we use by. To would mean the new figure was 20%.

cards.front: The data covers the period between 2000 ____ 2010.
cards.why: Between always pairs with and. From pairs with to.
Interested always takes in, and the verb after it uses the -ing form.

cards.front: City life is very different ____ village life.
cards.why: Different takes from. Its opposite, similar, takes to.

cards.front: This plan will contribute to ____ traffic.
cards.why: In contribute to, to is a preposition, so the verb after it takes -ing.
